questions.prompt: Why are server tools registered on the tool registry, not called by the client directly?
options: So they pass the same pre-execute, approval and post-execute checks as built-in tools
Because the client cannot send tools/call
So the server can see the model's history
questions.explanation: A registered tool runs through the same pipeline as every other tool, so an outside program gets no fewer checks.

questions.prompt: Server docs offers search.pages. Why does its public name end with a 12-character hash?
options: Every MCP tool name ends with a hash
The name is longer than 64 characters
Cleaning the dot to _ could make it equal to the name of a tool called search_pages
The hash is the server's password
questions.explanation: Cleaning changed the name, so two different raw names could print the same public name. The hash of server and raw name keeps them apart.

questions.prompt: Registering the third of five server tools fails. What does the model see?
options: Four tools, without the failed one
questions.explanation: The loop disposes the tools it already registered, so a server's tools appear all together or not at all.
